title: Local anesthesia
what: A shot or cream that numbs a small part of your body. You stay awake, but you feel no pain in that spot.
why: For small operations and procedures: dental fillings and extractions, mole removal, stitches.
duration: usually lasts from 1 to a few hours
tell_doctor: How you handled numbing shots before
Your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor decides what to do
Heart disease or blood pressure problems
If you are pregnant or breastfeeding

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can usually eat a light meal beforehand. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Take your regular medicines as usual, unless your doctor says otherwise.

prepare.title: How you feel
prepare.text: Come well rested. If you feel very nervous, tell the doctor.

steps: The doctor cleans the skin or the inside of your mouth
Sometimes a numbing gel or spray goes on first
The doctor gives a shot with a thin needle
You wait a few minutes until the spot goes numb
The doctor checks that you feel no pain, then starts
feel: A quick prick and a few seconds of stinging
Then numbness. The spot may feel strange or swollen
You feel touch and pressure, but not pain
If it starts to hurt, say so. The doctor will give more numbing medicine
after: Numbness usually wears off in 1 to 3 hours
Until then, protect the spot. Do not bite your cheek or lip
Do not eat hot food while your mouth is numb
If numbness lasts more than a day, tell your doctor
red_flags: Trouble breathing, a swollen face, or a rash all over: call emergency services
Severe dizziness, a pounding heart, or seizures: call emergency services

faq.q: Do you feel anything with local anesthesia?
faq.a: Yes, pressure and touch. There should be no pain. If it hurts, tell the doctor.

faq.q: How long until the numbness wears off?
faq.a: Usually 1 to 3 hours. It depends on the medicine and where the shot was given.
